title: ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Producers on Episode 2’s Surprise Kaley Cuoco Cameo As an Alternate Penny
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers from “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” Season 1 Episode 2, now streaming on HBO Max.

	“Stuart Fails t
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers from “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” Season 1 Episode 2, now streaming on HBO Max.

	“Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” Episode 2 was chock full of cameos and guest stars — but saved the biggest one, at least for “The Big Bang Theory” fans, until near the end of the episode: The return of Kaley Cuoco as Penny. But a very different Penny.


	In the episode, “Spoiler: Zack’s In This One,” Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Kripke (John Ross Bowie) and Bert (Brian Posehn) land in a much less apocalyptic Pasadena than the one they just escaped — and in this world, Kripke is no longer a vicious ruler (he plays off killing Raj in the previous world: “There are two possibilities. One, the world we were just in no longer exists. In which case I did not kill Raj. Two, that world and this world are part of an infinite number of worlds, in which case I killed one in an infinite number of Rajes. Mathematically, a rounding error.”)
	

	But in the happy-go-lucky, peaceful new universe they land in, things aren’t as cracked up as they seem: The characters all have a device planted on the back of their necks, sending them an electric shock whenever they argue or get angry. And for this crew, with Stuart and Kripke going at it, that’s a lot.



	

									colin remas brown
	



	Denise (Lauren Lapkus) didn’t make the trip through the wormhole with them, so Stuart goes looking for her — and finds her with her new beau, Gary (Tommy Walker). Meanwhile, hoping to find Sheldon and Leonard to get some answers, Kripke and Bert head to Caltech, where they find an extremely unhelpful receptionist (Riki Lindhome, who originally played Dr. Ramona Nowitzki on “The Big Bang Theory”). 
	



	

	



	The receptionist angers Kripke and Bert so much that they are picked up by the police — along with Stuart, who had also been arrested. They’re sent to a reprogramming facility, where they watch a video hosted by Christine Baranski, playing herself. (On “The Big Bang Theory,” Baranski played Leonard’s mother, Dr. Beverly Hofstadter.)

	After thirty months of rehabilitation, the trio are finally released — and immediately kidnapped by a resistance group. That organization meets inside a warehouse, where we discover it’s led by. Penny (played by Cuoco). But this isn’t the Penny we remember from “The Big Bang Theory.” This one is a badass soldier/leader, who can’t stop slapping Stuart, Kripke and Bert. Denise is there too, as is Penny’s ex-boyfriend Zack (Brian Thomas Smith).

	“A big part of it was offering them a challenge to do something entirely different,” co-creator and executive producer Chuck Lorre says of bringing back some of the original “The Big Bang Theory” cast members in new versions of their characters. “As you’ve seen in Episode 2, Kaley’s not playing the server in the Cheesecake Factory. It’s still Penny, and now she’s a badass guerrilla leader. That was part of the design from the very beginning. In a multiverse environment, these characters could recur as themselves, but with an entirely different backstory.”

	On “The Big Bang Theory,” which ran from 2007 to 2019, Penny moves into an apartment next door to Leonard (Johnny Galecki) and Sheldon (Jim Parsons); as the series progressed, Penny and Leonard became a couple and eventually married.

	At the end of Episode 2 of “Stuart Fails,” Penny’s secret hideout is discovered by the authoritarian bots that control human emotions, and just in time Stuart, Denise, Kripke and Bert fire up the Leonard, Sheldon and Howard quantum interference device that takes them to another universe: And next episode, it looks like things get a little magic.

schema.headline: ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Producers on Episode 2’s Surprise Kaley Cuoco Cameo As an Alternate Penny

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: Sadie Sink Is [SPOILER]. How Her Role Sets Up Marvel’s Next Reboot
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ now playing in theaters.

	After months of speculation about wh
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ now playing in theaters.

	After months of speculation about who Sadie Sink is playing in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” the movie has finally hit theaters and Spidey fans can see for themselves which comic-book character she’s bringing to life

	As many people predicted, the red-headed “Stranger Things” star is in fact playing Jean Grey, one of the original members of the X-Men. We’ll no doubt be seeing her in the MCU’s planned “X-Men” movie, though no details on its cast or release have been announced.
	

	Sink’s identity is shrouded in mystery as “Brand New Day” begins, and her face isn’t revealed until roughly halfway through the film. Tom Holland’s Spider-Man begins investigating a new villain on the loose in New York City who has the power to possess bystanders’ bodies (as long as they’re less than 33 feet away). She uses her abilities to “jump” between between people’s minds and attempt to break into the headquarters for the Department of Damage Control. The organization, which is responsible for cleaning up the messes after superhero battles, has something that Jean wants locked inside a vault.


	After a failed break-in attempt using a possessed Scorpion (Michael Mando), Sink turns to a stronger, larger and greener wrecking ball to get inside of Damage Control: the Hulk. She takes control of Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner and removes the inhibitor device that prevents him from turning into the Hulk. Spider-Man teams up with Jon Bernthal’s Punisher to take down the green giant and stop the him from destroying the Damage Control skyscraper entirely. Jean manages to break into the secret vault, but she’s tranquilized and apprehended by Tramell Tillman’s Damage Control CEO Bill Metzger.
	

	It’s here that Damage Control is revealed as the real villainous organization in the movie. Metzger and his team hold Jean hostage and run tests on her to understand how her psychic powers work. A flashback reveals that Jean had an older sister named Sara who could also possess people’s minds. One day in the park, Sara gets abducted by Damage Control officers, and she possesses Jean’s mind to run away and save her younger sister. When Jean is imprisoned, she realizes she’s locked in the same cell that was used to hold Sara, who had died while being tested on by Damage Control. Jean overpowers their restraints and creates a gigantic psychic bubble that freezes in place nearly everyone in New York City.

	Spider-Man is the only person who can overcome Jean’s psychic powers, and he’s able to reason with her to drop her vendetta against Damage Control. While Jean probes Spidey’s mind and lives through a tender memory he has of his late Aunt May (Marisa Tomei), Punisher is miles away lining up a sniper rifle to take out the mutant threat. As he fires the bullet, Spider-Man pushes Jean out of the way at the last second, but is hit by the gunshot himself. A devastated Punisher rescues Spider-Man and brings him to a hospital, where he eventually recovers; Jean had been using her powers to keep the hero alive, but she leaves before Spidey can say goodbye.

	In the final moments of the movie, Jean is seen riding a bus out of the city. Could she be heading upstate to the Xavier School for Gifted Youngsters? The famous mutant school is located in Westchester, and the fall foliage suggests school may be in session soon. There aren’t any references to the X-Men or other mutants in “Brand New Day,” but it seems clear that this isn’t the last we’ll see of Sink. It also seems like Damage Control may be morphed into a more evil corporation that’s anti-mutant in the future.

	The “Stranger Things” breakout star is the third actor to take on the famous telekinetic mutant in live-action. In Fox’s previous “X-Men” movies, Jean had been played by Famke Janssen in the original film trilogy Then in the prequel series, “Game of Thrones” star Sophie Turner had taken on a younger version of the mutant. 

	Now, it seems that Sink will be part of the next generation of X-Men in the MCU. We’ve seen several “X-Men” actors reprise their Fox roles, like Hugh Jackman as Wolverine, Ryan Reynolds as Deadpool, Patrick Stewart as Prof. Charles Xavier and Kelsey Grammer as Beast. In “Doomsday,” Stewart and Grammer will be joined by James Marsden as Cyclops, Ian McKellen as Magneto, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler and Channing Tatum as Gambit. After living in their own X-universe, the stars will be thrust into the MCU, joining forces with the Avengers and Fantastic Four to take on Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom. With Sink’s casting, it seems like the MCU is prepping a new, younger cast of X-Men to join their sprawling universe of heroes.

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: Sadie Sink Is [SPOILER]. How Her Role Sets Up Marvel’s Next Reboot

title: Boy George Drops Out of London ‘Jesus Christ Superstar’ Production Following Backlash to Pro-Israel Song
description: Boy George has dropped out of a London production of “Jesus Christ Superstar” just days after releasing the controversial pro-Israel song “We Will D
body:
Boy George has dropped out of a London production of “Jesus Christ Superstar” just days after releasing the controversial pro-Israel song “We Will Dance Again.”

	Paul Kemsley, George’s manager, released a statement on social media that he had decided that the Culture Club singer would no longer appear in the production at the London Palladium. “The decision has been made with the utmost respect for the producers, the creative team and the entire company,” he wrote, apologizing to fans who had purchased tickets in hopes of seeing the show.
	

	“George has never been afraid to stand by his personal convictions, and I have always respected him for that. Equally, I believe it is my responsibility to make decisions that are in the best interests of my artist while also showing respect to others. In this instance, I felt it was right to step aside, allowing the production to remain the focus, while ensuring everyone involved can move forward with mutual respect and goodwill.”



	George was scheduled to join the cast of “Jesus Chris Superstar” as King Herod from August 3-15. He was set to star alongside Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Richard Armitage, Simon Russell Beale, Layton Williams and Julian Clary.

	Earlier this week, George drew ire after posting a pro-Israel song on social media with the Hebrew title “עוד נרקוד,” which translates to “We Will Dance Again.” On the song, the 65-year-old sings, “You say genocide, I say war / When you’re attacked, what’s what the army’s for / Does it get ugly? / You bet it does / When I know you wanna kill every last one of us.” He later explained that he made the track using AI.
	

	Though George is yet to reference his exit from the musical, he did acknowledge the backlash to “We Will Dance Again” on Thursday afternoon. “It doesn’t matter what I think or you think,” he wrote on X. “When will you realise you’re doing NOTHING! It’s a fucking joke. I am even falling out with Jewish friends. The madness knows no bounds.”

schema.headline: Boy George Drops Out of London ‘Jesus Christ Superstar’ Production Following Backlash to Pro-Israel Song

title: Disney Expected to Sell 50% Stake in A+E to Hearst for More Than $1 Billion
description: Disney is getting ready to shed its ownership stake in A+E Global Media, the cable-focused programmer it has owned jointly with Hearst for more than
body:
Disney is getting ready to shed its ownership stake in A+E Global Media, the cable-focused programmer it has owned jointly with Hearst for more than a decade.

	Disney will sell its 50% stake in A+E Global Media (formerly known as A+E Networks) to Hearst, in a transaction valued at over $1 billion, a source familiar with the plans confirmed. The sale, giving Hearst 100% control over A+E going forward, is expected to be finalized next week and announced in conjunction with Disney’s quarterly earnings on Aug. 5.
	

	Reps for Hearst, Disney and A+E did not immediately respond to requests for comment.


	In a blog post Thursday, LightShed Partners analyst Rich Greenfield, in a preview of Disney earnings, wrote, “We believe Disney will announce the sale of its 50% stake in A&E Networks to its joint venture partner, Hearst, in an all-cash transaction at a low single-digit EBITDA multiple.”

	Disney, in its 10-Q filing with the SEC for the March 2026 quarter, said its investment in A+E had a carrying value of approximately $2 billion. In accounting, “carrying value” is the original cost of an asset minus accumulated depreciation or amortization, per Investopedia. During the quarter, the media company took a $147 million charge for an impairment of its investment in A+E Global Media.

	Disney has been looking to sell its stake in A+E for at least a year. After Disney exits the joint venture, A+E Global Media president and chairman Paul Buccieri will continue to run the company, reporting to Hearst CEO Steve Swartz.

	A+E’s cable networks include A&E Network, Lifetime, History, Lifetime Movie Network, FYI and Vice TV. Its assets also encompass content units A+E Studios, A+E Factual Studio, A&E IndieFilms, A+E Global Media Digital as well as streaming apps including subscription-video services including Lifetime Movie Club,  Crime 360 and History Vault.
	

	In 2009, A&E Television Networks — then a partnership among Disney-ABC Television Group, Hearst and NBCUniversal — acquired Lifetime Entertainment Services. In 2012, NBCU sold its 15.8% stake in A&E Networks to Disney and Hearst.

schema.headline: Disney Expected to Sell 50% Stake in A+E to Hearst for More Than $1 Billion

title: Banijay Americas CEO Ben Samek to Oversee Merged Banijay/All3Media Operations in the U.S.
description: With the completion of the $8 billion merger between Banijay and All3Media, as expected Banijay Americas CEO Ben Samek is in line to oversee the com
body:
With the completion of the $8 billion merger between Banijay and All3Media, as expected Banijay Americas CEO Ben Samek is in line to oversee the combined company’s U.S. entity.

	News comes after Banijay and All3Media, which described their merger as “the world’s largest independent production company,” finalized their deal earlier this month. The newly renamed Banijay Entertainment will be based in London and jointly owned by Banijay Group and RedBird IMI, each holding a 50% stake. Jeff Zucker is chairman, Marco Bassetti is CEO and Jane Turton is deputy CEO.
	

	Samek has served as CEO of Banijay Americas since February 2023; before that, he had been president and chief operating officer of Banijay Americas since 2018. Banijay Americas’ many production labels include top unscripted producers such as Endemol Shine North America, Bunim/Murray Productions, Truly Original, 51 Minds, Authentic Entertainment, Endemol Shine Boomdog and Banijay Mexico. 


	Among Samek’s recent accomplishments, he spearheaded the expansion of “Somebody Feed Phil” from Netflix into a broader deal at YouTube. He’s also spearheaded an expansion in immersive experiences, taking IP into another realm.

	Before his roles at Banijay, served in a number of roles at Endemol USA and Endemol Shine North America, helping with the transition following Banijay’s acquisition of Endemol Shine Group. 

	Samek began his career at Bunim/Murray Productions and later won an Emmy as a producer on “The Amazing Race.” He then went on to become COO of 51 Minds Entertainment.

	Major Banijay Americas franchises under Samek’s domain include “Big Brother,” “MasterChef,” “MasterChef Junior,” “Below Deck,” “Below Deck Mediterranean,” “The Challenge,” “Deal or No Deal Island” and “Lego Masters.” All3Media Americas has been less active in recent years, but All3Media has a huge hit in the U.S. from its Studio Lambert subsidiary, Peacock’s “The Traitors.”

schema.headline: Banijay Americas CEO Ben Samek to Oversee Merged Banijay/All3Media Operations in the U.S.

title: ‘Wonder Man’ Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Speaks Out After Marvel Series Canceled: ‘That’s Life… Everything Will Shake Out’
description: “Wonder Man” star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II is speaking out about the surprise cancellation of the Marvel TV series, after it had been renewed for a sec
body:
“Wonder Man” star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II is speaking out about the surprise cancellation of the Marvel TV series, after it had been renewed for a second season on Disney+.

	“Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back for Season 2. (And if you don’t knowww, now ya knoww!” Abdul-Mateen wrote on Instagram, referencing Variety’s exclusive reporting, published earlier Thursday. “That’s life, right? Everything will shake out.” 
	

	Abdul-Mateen II starred in the comedy series as Simon Williams, an aspiring actor hiding his superpowers, opposite Ben Kingsley, who reprised his role as Trevor Slattery after previous MCU outings. “Wonder Man” was created by Destin Daniel Cretton and Andrew Guest, with Cretton also directing the first two episodes. Guest served as showrunner. The Season 1 cast also included X Mayo, Demetrius Grosse, Zlatko Burić, Arian Moayed, Josh Gad and Olivia Thirlby.


	“Wonder Man,” which began streaming in January, was received well by critics (a 91% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes). In her review for Variety, Alison Herman wrote, “Abdul-Mateen and Kingsley make their characters equally ridiculous and romantic, urged on by a motivation more intimate and individual than saving the world.” Then, in March, Disney announced the show had been renewed for Season 2; however, sources say a writers’ room was never opened. Earlier this month, Abdul-Mateen — already an Emmy-winning actor for “Watchmen” — earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series.

	Despite the change in fortunes, Abdul-Mateen put a positive spin on the news, thanking the audience who “watched, enjoyed and shared that they enjoyed the show” in some form or fashion. “The show worked. And that’s my favorite thing about it,” he wrote. “I could see it on the faces of the Youtube Reactors (because I watched along with y’all this time. Shoutout to y’all) and I can see in the messages I get saying how the show reminded some of you not to give up, and I feel it in the genuine love shared when I bump into some of you all during the day. So, thinking of you all today.”
	

	Concluding his note, Abdul-Mateen wrote: “I’m glad we got to be a part of something cool. Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the Emmys.”

	And there is hope that Marvel fans haven’t seen the last of Simon Williams or Trevor Slattery. According to an individual with knowledge of the situation, while “Wonder Man” is not proceeding with Season 2, the characters featured in the series could still appear in other Marvel projects in the future.

schema.headline: ‘Wonder Man’ Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Speaks Out After Marvel Series Canceled: ‘That’s Life… Everything Will Shake Out’

title: ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ Reveals Star Wars, ‘World of Warcraft’-Themed Tabletop Roleplaying Games as Part of New ‘Universes Beyond’ Collection
description: “Dungeons & Dragons” maker Wizards of the Coast announced the upcoming launch of Star Wars and “World of Warcraft“-themed tabletop role-playing game
body:
“Dungeons & Dragons” maker Wizards of the Coast announced the upcoming launch of Star Wars and “World of Warcraft“-themed tabletop role-playing game offerings during Gen Con 2026 on Thursday.

	Starting Nov. 17, the “WoW”-themed “D&D” book will allow players to “roll for Azeroth as they recreate their ‘World of Warcraft’ main character or roll a new alt and explore beloved zones, delve through familiar dungeons and face legendary foes from over 20 years of history for the ‘World of Warcraft’ franchise.” 
	

	An Icecrown Citadel Map Pack will also be available, featuring poster maps and tokens that can be used with a digital adventure that raises players four levels.


	The “World of Warcraft”-themed game, which is made in collaboration with video game developer Blizzard, will be the first in a line of “Universes Beyond” products from the “D&D” team. These new offerings will be based on outside IP, much like the “Universes Beyond” collections produced by fellow Wizards of the Coast brand Magic: The Gathering.

	In 2027, Wizards will release a Star Wars-themed “D&D” gameplay book that takes place in “the Season of Rebellion” as another “Universes Beyond” edition.

	“‘World of Warcraft’ and ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ are both built on a powerful idea: give players a world full of possibility, then let them make the story their own,” said Holly Longdale, the executive producer and vice president of “World of Warcraft” at Blizzard Entertainment. “Azeroth has always meant something different to everyone who steps into it, whether it’s built upon the heroes they become, the friends they find or the choices they make along the way.”
	

	The “D&D: World of Warcraft” and Star Wars collaboration news was revealed during Gen Con Thursday, along with the announcement of D&D Icons, a creative initiative bringing D&D creatives to work on fan-favorite settings, including Dragonlance. Margaret Weis, Tracy Hickman, Luke Gygax and RA Salvatore are among those helming the content program.

	Additional announcements include the return of the Dark Sun setting, a new mobile experience for “D&D Beyond” and a partnership program to bring TTRPG support for campaign settings. Theo Solomon will also be joining the cast of the D&D actual play YouTube show “Dungeon Masters” for Campaign 3.

schema.headline: ‘Dungeons & Dragons’ Reveals Star Wars, ‘World of Warcraft’-Themed Tabletop Roleplaying Games as Part of New ‘Universes Beyond’ Collection

title: Veteran Reality Exec Mike Darnell Seals Overall Deal at Netflix, Where He’ll Also Provide Guidance on the Streamer’s Unscripted Slate
description: The dark prince of reality TV has re-emerged. Mike Darnell has inked an exclusive, multi-year overall deal with Netflix, where he will also consult
body:
The dark prince of reality TV has re-emerged. Mike Darnell has inked an exclusive, multi-year overall deal with Netflix, where he will also consult on the platform’s unscripted slate. He’ll work closely with Netflix nonfiction series & sports vice president Brandon Riegg, who was instrumental in recruiting Darnell to the streamer.

	According to insiders, Darnell will be tasked to “provide strategic creative guidance across the unscripted slate, collaborate with the team on creative development and shape new ideas across the portfolio.”
	

	Darnell had previously spent a decade at Warner Bros. Television Group before leaving in 2023, a move he decided to make after a restructuring would have altered his role at the company. 


	Darnell joined Warner Bros. in 2013 after a legendary 18-year run at Fox, where his reputation was cemented as the reality kingpin behind TV phenomenon “American Idol,” as well as juicy TV favorites like “Who Wants to Marry a Multi-Millionaire” and “Temptation Island,” as well as in-your-face fare including “Joe Millionaire,” “Alien Autopsy: Fact or Fiction,” “The Swan,” “When Animals Attack” and “Man vs. Beast.” (At Fox he also helped shepherd animated hits “Family Guy” and “Futurama.”)

	He continued that streak at Warner Bros., doubling the studio’s unscripted output and overseeing hundreds of series on broadcast, cable, streamers and first-run syndication. His oversight included NBC’s “The Voice,” ABC’s “The Bachelor,” “The Bachelorette” and “Bachelor in Paradise.” He also launched the studio’s “The Jennifer Hudson Show” talker in syndication.  
	

	Darnell expanded Warner Bros. TV Group in digital with Ellentube and games (with the app Heads Up!), and expanded the studio into high-end documentaries with a slate that includes projects at Netflix, Apple TV+, Paramount+, HBO Sports and Max.

	Darnell’s arrival comes as Jeff Gaspin exited his role as Netflix‘s VP of unscripted series in July after a little more than two years. 

	Deadline first broke news of Darnell’s appointment.

schema.headline: Veteran Reality Exec Mike Darnell Seals Overall Deal at Netflix, Where He’ll Also Provide Guidance on the Streamer’s Unscripted Slate

title: As Outfest Rebuilds, What Will the Future of L.A.’s Staple LGBTQ+ Film Festival Look Like?
description:
Outfest looked a little different this past weekend.

	Instead of the usual 11-day window over the summer, the festivities ran for four days from Ju
body:
Outfest looked a little different this past weekend.

	Instead of the usual 11-day window over the summer, the festivities ran for four days from July 23-26, with screenings and conversations held at the Los Angeles LGBT Center’s Renberg Theatre in Hollywood. The program featured over 30 films and shorts, headlined by Gregg Araki’s “I Want Your Sex,” Brydie O’Connor’s “Barbara Forever” and Alexandria Stapleton’s “The Brittney Griner Story.”
	

	OutfestNEXT is all part of Outfest’s strategy to strategically scale down after a two-year hiatus, caused by financial troubles, a legal battle with a former executive director and unionization of the organization’s workforce that culminated in mass layoffs. “It really left a hole when we weren’t doing our traditional summer festival,” interim executive director Christopher Racster tells Variety. “It is a chance for us to experiment.”


	But most screenings held at the Renberg Theatre, which holds 183 people, were sold out or on standby, and conversations with filmmakers and members of the community continued in the bustling courtyard long after the credits rolled. Clearly, there was a hole in the heart of L.A.’s queer film community without a yearly festival like Outfest bringing people together.

	“I call it the unfortunate opportunity,” Racster says of the “perfect storm” that caused the organization to shutter. He references the SAG-AFTRA strikes starting in July 2023 that made it nearly impossible for donors to continue their contributions, the Dylan Mulvaney Bud Light incident that led corporations to “retract” their support of queer organizations, and “management issues” within Outfest’s own organization.
	

	As Outfest looks to rebuild and reestablish itself as a mainstay L.A. film festival, a new board of directors was appointed last September to spearhead the organization, led by president Lucas Bailey, who joined Outfest in January 2024 after working as an attorney for NBCUniversal, Peacock and Netflix.

	“I won’t say that it’s been an easy couple of years. We upset a lot of people in our community, and we have done our best with this new board to repair things,” Bailey says.

	He adds: “I also like the fact that we’ve now got a spectrum of ages. I’m trying to bring in younger people who are early-to-mid level career, who have the energy and time to help shape this next chapter.”

	“Our focus has been on clear and transparent financials, and a sustainable business model,” Racster says. “The sad thing is, with all nonprofits or any organizations that’ve been around as long, you go through cycles. There’s no one who’s stable for 45 years. It’s just unfortunate that it happened and that people were injured in the process.”

	Racster, who previously served as Outfest’s executive director from 2011 to 2019, says he was able to bring back two-thirds of the staff that he originally hired.

	“That makes me feel great because they understand us from the inside,” he says. “It allows them to have an opportunity to have some agency that they haven’t had over the past couple of the years.”

	While Racster, Outfest’s only full-time staff member, says he’d like to continue hosting OutfestNEXT twice a year, “growing it beyond just that time frame” is a long-term priority to attract more press, agents, managers and distributors.

	The organization also does one-off screenings throughout the year. In April, Outfest hosted a screening of “The Other Two” actor Noam Ash’s new film “Bookends,” which he wrote and starred in alongside F. Murray Abraham and Charlie Barnett.

	“We had our screening sell out in a couple of hours, which I think is really a testament to the audience the festival has built, and how much hunger there is for these films,” Ash says, who was part of the festival’s host committee to help spread the word about Outfest’s return to summer programming.

	“What people don’t recognize is that when places like Outfest go quiet for a couple of years because of our own problems, you miss a whole pipeline of people getting their start and getting their first opportunity to exhibit,” Bailey says, adding that Outfest alumni have gone on to screen their work at festivals like Sundance thanks to their long-standing relationship.
	

	For performers and screenwriters on the rise like Ash, festivals like Outfest are not just an opportunity to connect with the larger LGBTQ+ community, but a chance to get noticed by executives and dealmakers; “Bookends” is currently finalizing a theatrical distribution deal after playing the festival circuit, including stops at Frameline and the Santa Barbara International Film Festival.

	Ash says, “On a professional level, it is so important that there is someone exhibiting these films in Los Angeles. It’s where the people who, in many respects, decide what gets made in Hollywood, get to come and see how these stories are affecting change and how much they resonate with people. In that way, it also has implications that reach much further than just the local community. The decisions that are made in this town affect the landscape across the country and the world.”

	Outfest’s senior programmer Daniel Crooke notes that the programming team has gotten smaller, now led by a four-person team. But he remains “emboldened” by the turnout at the first edition of OutfestNEXT back in November, which was presented by HBO Max and featured a 25th anniversary screening of Greg Berlanti’s directorial debut “Broken Hearts Club.”

	“My main learning from OutfestNEXT last year was that people are so hungry to sit in a theater together,” Crooke says. “Honestly, as soon as we wrapped last year, we immediately started talking about how we were going to run this thing back and do it again.”

	Connecting influential queer filmmakers like Berlanti and Araki to the emerging filmmakers of today is an essential part of Outfest’s mission.

	“One of the really exciting things for me, when I’m looking at this new generations of queer and trans filmmakers, is that the fingerprints of Gregg Araki are all over them,” Crooke says. “I think about a film we played, ‘Sparks,’ which is about a renegade group of indie filmmakers in small-town Nevada. There is a punk poetry to that film, an unapologetic spirit that feels so tied to what Araki has done his whole career. It’s exciting to have a pairing like that in the program.”



	

					Gregg Araki presented his new film “I Want Your Sex” at OutfestNEXT.
									Chloe Kern
	



	As the festival searches for new means of funding, Racster is treating Outfest’s shuttering and the current political climate as a “good wake-up call” for where queer-led organizations need to look if they want to stick around.
	

	“We were very reliant on corporations, especially entertainment corporations. And when we’re in the middle of mergers, suddenly, two studios that support you with two different checks become one studio and one check,” he says, while noting that studios like Netflix, Warner Bros., Sony, NBCUniversal and Paramount have “maintained” their support in spite of the volatile political climate.

	Bailey says “once DEI comes back,” he wants Outfest to re-partner with different resource groups and bring exclusive screenings and panels to employees.

	“Once we get more funding that we can allocate, I’d love to pursue that because that’s when you start to build partnerships with corporations that are interested in supporting the arts,” he continues.

	While Outfest’s exact next steps remain to be seen, Racster and his board of directors are currently focused on building out the org’s educational opportunities for emerging filmmakers, including a producers lab and the return of Outfest Fusion, which spotlights films by queer filmmakers of color.

	“You can corner me and ask hard questions if you want to. That’s the best way to figure it out,” Racster says. “For the future, I want us to play a really critical role in helping our filmmakers manage the transition that’s going on in the industry right now and build sustainable, long-term careers. That is some of the biggest service we can do, not just to our storytellers, but to the industry right now when so many people are struggling.”

schema.headline: As Outfest Rebuilds, What Will the Future of L.A.’s Staple LGBTQ+ Film Festival Look Like?

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Early Cut ‘Took Notes From Random People’ at Test Screenings and ‘We Hated It,’ Says Tom Holland: ‘It Totally Didn’t Work’
description: Tom Holland said in an interview with Quotable on the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” press tour that one of the worst cuts he saw of the movie was shap
body:
Tom Holland said in an interview with Quotable on the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” press tour that one of the worst cuts he saw of the movie was shaped by test screenings. 

	“We’ve seen loads of different cuts of this movie, and one of the cuts, they took all of the notes from all of the random people [at test screenings] who saw the film,” Holland said. “And then they changed the movie, and we watched it, and we hated it. It totally didn’t work. It was what the people were asking for, but it wasn’t quite what we wanted as the creatives. But they learned lessons from that experience, so a movie can change in a thousand different ways in the edit room.”
	

	Test screenings have become a routine step in the studio moviemaking process. “Star Wars” creator George Lucas recently made headlines for speaking out against them. He told A Rabbit’s Foot (via IGN) that Hollywood’s over-reliance on focus groups has created studio movies dictated entirely by fans over filmmakers.


	“I don’t like focus groups,” Lucas told the publication. “The audience doesn’t know what they want to see. If they don’t like a character, that’s interesting, and as a filmmaker I want to find out why. But when the studios hear that, they take the wrong message. They let the audience actually make the movie. Of course, now they go crazy with that. Now, it’s all about what the fans think. That isn’t how you make the movie. You make a movie by finding someone that knows how to make movies, that has a story to tell and is passionate about it.”

	Maggie Gyllenhaal notably revealed earlier this year that test screenings for “The Bride!” took her to task over the movie’s depiction of violence and sexual violence. James Gunn test screened “Superman” and discovered that audiences opposed the moment when David Corenswet’s Man of Steel decides to save a squirrel as Metropolis is being attacked by a rampaging Kaiju monster. Gunn refused to listen.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opens in theaters July 31. Watch Holland and his co-stars’ full interview with Quotable in the video below.

title: Husband of North Carolina Woman Who Vanished On Caribbean Vacation Speaks Out
description:
Missing North Carolina Mom
                          Husband Says No Foul Play
body:
Missing North Carolina Mom
                          Husband Says No Foul Play
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The husband of a North Carolina woman who vanished while on vacation in the Caribbean says there appears to be no foul play ... and he claims authorities agree.
      
    
            There's a website dedicated to finding Elizabeth "Liz" Waddell ... and her husband, Cailen Waddell, posted a message saying "family, local authorities, the U.S. Embassy, and others here in Grenada" all concur a crime likely didn't occur.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... surveillance footage shows Liz swimming off Grand Anse Beach near her Airbnb in Grenada on July 22, while on a trip with her friend.
      

            The video shows her walking along the shore before jumping off a jetty into the water ... and after about 10 minutes, she swims away and out of frame.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cailen, who flew down on July 24 to help look for his wife, says the missing person investigation will continue.
      
    
            He's encouraging anyone with information -- even the smallest detail -- to come forward.
